title: What Luxury Buyers Actually Notice (It Is Not the Marble)
seoTitle: What Luxury Buyers Notice (It Is Not the Marble)
description: Developers spend millions on marble that luxury buyers barely notice. The three things buyers do notice, and why most presale material never shows them.
answer: Luxury buyers rarely notice the marble. They notice three things: the view from their bed when they wake up, the flow between the rooms of their unit, and the light in the living room in the morning and at sunset. Most developers never show buyers this information, so buyers are left guessing about the things they care about most.
body:
There is something that drives me crazy in luxury development. Developers spend millions on marble finishes, and the buyers they are trying to impress do not even notice it. The budget goes into materials, while the things buyers actually care about stay invisible until it is too late to show them.

## Why the marble does not sell the unit

Marble is expected in a luxury building. When every project in the same price range has premium finishes, the finishes stop being a reason to choose one unit over another. A buyer walks past the stone and asks a different kind of question: what will it feel like to live here every day?

That question is not answered by a material sample. It is answered by the experience of the space itself.

## The three things luxury buyers notice

In my experience, these are the three things that matter most to a luxury buyer:

1. **The view from their bed.** The first thing they see when they wake up, every morning, for years. Not the view from the rooftop, the view from their own bedroom.
2. **The flow between rooms.** How the unit moves from the entrance to the living room, to the kitchen, to the bedroom. Whether the layout feels open and natural or broken up.
3. **The light.** The morning light in the unit, and the sunset in the living room. Orientation decides this, and no finish can replace it.

These are the moments a buyer imagines when they picture their new home. They are emotional, and they are specific to one unit.

## Most developers never show this information

Here is the problem. A typical presale package shows lobbies, amenities and a few beautiful renderings, often of the best unit in the building. It almost never shows the view from the bed in unit 1204, the walk through that exact layout, or where the sun will be at six in the evening.

When buyers cannot see these things, they guess. And when a buyer is guessing about the things they care about most, they slow down, ask for more time, or walk away.

## What to show instead

If you are a developer preparing your next launch, shift part of the attention from materials to experience:

- Show the real view from the bedroom of each unit, not only from the top floor.
- Show how the rooms connect, so buyers can understand the flow of their own layout.
- Show the light at different times of day, especially morning and sunset.
- Make this information available for every unit, so each buyer can see their own home.

The marble is still part of the product. It is just not what closes the sale. The view, the flow and the light are what buyers remember, and they are what you need to show.
takeaways: Developers spend millions on marble that luxury buyers often do not even notice.
Luxury buyers notice the view from their bed when they wake up.
They notice the flow between the rooms of their unit.
They notice the morning light and the sunset in the living room.
Most developers never show this information, so buyers are left guessing.
faq: What do luxury home buyers care about most?

In my experience, they care most about how it feels to live in the unit: the view from the bedroom, the flow between rooms and the natural light through the day. Premium finishes are expected, so they rarely decide the sale.
Do expensive finishes help sell luxury condos?
They are part of what buyers expect at that price, but they are rarely the reason a buyer chooses one unit over another. The view, the layout and the light usually matter more.
How can developers show buyers the view from a unit before it is built?
By giving buyers unit-specific information, such as the real view from each room and how the light enters at different times of day, instead of only renderings of the best unit in the building.
Why does orientation matter so much in a luxury unit?
Orientation decides the morning light and the sunset in the living room. It cannot be changed after the building is designed, and buyers feel it every day.
